PeacockDB benchmark results — per dataset, a table at tp1_single, one row per query, with every device but h200 beside DuckDB. Below it, collapsed, the Modes: a table per device, its modes side by side under each measure. PeacockDB's times are device-side, in ms: the total is load plus execute. The peak is the accountant's peak, a lower bound on device memory, in GiB. A load marked unpinned was read without the pinned host cache: its section's pinned_cache is off, or the section predates the cache.

Sirius's total is the wall time around the statement and an Arrow fetch of its result, in ms: the second-smallest of the timed runs after one warm-up, from the parquet bytes pinned in Sirius's host cache. On some rows Sirius's log counts reads outside the pin (likely bloom filters) inside the timed runs. h100-80gb-hbm3, tpcds sf40: Sirius 8d17afec481c56903b61b74a9787423b470298a1, DuckDB 1.5.6, libcudf 26.08.01, driver 580.173.02, device NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3; h100-80gb-hbm3, tpch sf40: Sirius 8d17afec481c56903b61b74a9787423b470298a1, DuckDB 1.5.6, libcudf 26.08.01, driver 580.173.02, device NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3.

DuckDB's time is one DuckDB CLI process's wall time: the process started, the database opened and the query run, over warm native storage, the second-smallest of its runs, in ms. The floor is SELECT 1 timed the same way, what each time holds besides its query: duckdb-cpu128, tpcds sf40: DuckDB 1.5.4, 128 threads, host computeinstance-e01t2mm4265y8x88ey, floor 36 ms; duckdb-cpu128, tpch sf40: DuckDB 1.5.4, 128 threads, host computeinstance-e01t2mm4265y8x88ey, floor 30 ms.
